title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
MDS here we go.


This program is a whirlwind.
Without exageration, these past 2 weeks have already been the biggest academic challenge I’ve faced in entire my life. I’m commuting for 90 minutes to be on campus from 8:00am to 4:00pm and working all throughout on any of my 4 lab assignments due by the end of the week. And our exams are already around the corner. In week 3.
It’s been a challenge trying to keep morale up at the beginning of the program. It was quite demoralizing in week 1 to have to ask around about how to use the terminal to open a document when it felt like everyone was already moving ahead to their real work. It’s still demoralizing now to watch people complete their assignments at double the pace that I’m able to right now. Even if it might not get any easier, I know I’m going to get better at it. It’ll even out eventually if I keep pushing.
At the same time, and on a more positive note, I feel like I have finally found my people. All of us are data nerds speaking the same language and it’s why we’re here. As soon as we get pasat the basics of how to use the terminal and R and Python, we’ll be able to dig into real data science and learn about how to make predictions and models. It’s just around the corner and it has me so excited to see what’s to come during the rest of this program.

text: Before data science, I joined Canucks Sports and Entertainment as Warehouse Intern helping to feed 18,000 screaming fans. title: About
text:
Where I Hope to Go
With the MDS program, I’m hoping to develop my skills in data science to complement the operational knowledge and policy experience I developed from my Sauder BCom and work in the BC Government. My goal is to leverage data science to improve public services. Whether that’s by improving transportation infrastructure, modelling economic growth, or optimizing emergency response times, I’ll go where I can make an impact by using data to make life better for the people who rely on those services.

What is the average horsepower and fuel efficiency for each cylinder count?

#Finding average horsepower and fuel efficiency for cars of each cylinder count
cyl_avg <- cars |>
  group_by(cyl) |>
  summarise(
    avg_hp = mean(hp),
    avg_mpg = mean(mpg)
  )
